title: Design spike only: drive the user's own signed-in Chrome through an attested extension backend, behind per-tab consent
summary: Only after the multi-backend work in R-t2-03-09: ship an MV3 extension with debugger permission and a relay to Quarry (native messaging or a hosted bridge) that registers a 'user_browser' BrowserBackend with isolated_egress=false and security_evidence=false. Allow it only for interactive (non-background) runs with explicit per-tab user consent, a visible indicator, and Quarry relaying and recording every action the Model proposes. || Write an ADR and prototype scope for an extension plus native-host bridge that lets the user's own Chrome/Edge profile act as a Quarry executor kind. To keep the Model-proposes/Quarry-executes rule, the extension would only run actions that Quarry has already validated against a BrowserBroker grant and would return receipts to Quarry; it must not take instructions from the Model Plane or the SPA directly. Do not start implementation until the connector-to-browser bridge and Quarry profile login hand-off have shipped.
whyItMatters: It is the only route to SSO-protected enterprise apps and the user's signed-in state without importing credentials, and it delivers the 'it uses my browser' experience that Codex offers. It is high value but conflicts with Verevon's governed-egress model, so it is a later, deliberate product decision. || Users want agents to use sites where they are already signed in, without re-authentication. It is an alternative to R-t2-10-01 for authenticated access, but it weakens the server-side containment that makes ZDR, egress proof and grants enforceable.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex native messaging host plus extension using chrome.debugger (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-010, SRC)
others: Codex browser plugin (Chrome extension plus Rust native messaging host bridged to the app server)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: MV3 extension with the debugger permission attaches chrome.debugger to tabs the user shares; a native messaging host (or hosted WebSocket bridge) relays CDP commands from the agent service; the extension enforces per-tab consent and shows an indicator. || Merged items add: Extension to native host over stdin/stdout; native host to app server over a local WebSocket or named pipe; the manifest pins extension ids and required protocol versions with explicit update-required errors; tab-context assets are written in bounded chunks.

verevonToday.gap: No extension or user-browser bridge; login is handled only by persisted profiles and human takeover of a leased Chromium. Any bridge has to be designed around the rule that the browser client never receives CDP endpoints or Quarry tokens. || No extension or native host; all browsing is a remote leased Chromium in Quarry. This is deliberate and enforces ZDR, egress control and grants server-side.

approach: Spike, not build: measure how much of the need is already met by the secret bridge (F-t2-024) and takeover login into scoped profiles, then decide in an ADR. If pursued, it is one more backend in the multi-backend abstraction (F-t2-059) with its own reduced capability set, because it gives up egress containment, SSRF guarantees and ZDR evidence. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-12] Frontend Plane: extension and consent UI. Ingestion Plane: 'user_browser' BrowserBackend with capability flags set false for containment and ZDR evidence so policy can refuse it for ZDR and background runs; the Model proposes and Quarry relays and records; the Model Plane approval grants (sensitive actions) still apply. Treat as a separate product decision with security review before any build. || [R-t2-10-08] Frontend Plane (extension, distribution) plus Ingestion Plane (a new executor kind registered with Quarry) plus Model Plane (BrowserBroker grant). Start with an ADR; a prototype would register the extension as a lease provider attested by a device key, with egress proof and ZDR weaker than remote Chromium and clearly labelled.
dependencies: Extension store review and enterprise policy deployment
F-t2-024 (secret bridge) and Quarry profile login hand-off, to measure how much of the need they already meet
risks: Loses egress containment and SSRF guarantees; ZDR evidence cannot be guaranteed; extension store review and enterprise rollout; prompt-injected pages act with the user's real sessions. || Exposes the user's full signed-in profile to agent actions; hard to audit; conflicts with Quarry executes and with ZDR/egress guarantees; extension permissions and store review burden.

verevon.exactGap: No extension, native host or user-browser executor exists (a repo search for chrome.debugger, nativeMessaging and manifest_version matches only a plan JSON); all browsing is a Quarry-leased chromiumoxide with one agent driver in AppState, and persisted profiles plus human takeover cover signed-in access. The product owner ruled on 2026-09-28 that the user's own Chrome and its logins are not driven and the 2026-10-01 parity audit records it as parked or ruled out. Quarry's fail-closed gate (require_isolated_agent_egress) refuses any agent driver without isolated_egress and security_evidence, so a user_browser backend flagged false on both would be refused unless that gate is redesigned.

verevon.constraints: Direct conflict with an owner ruling (2026-09-28) and with the architecture rules: the extension must not take instructions from Model Plane or the SPA, since the Model proposes and Quarry executes or rejects; the SPA never sees CDP endpoints or Quarry tokens; a user_browser backend gives up isolated egress, SSRF guarantees and ZDR evidence, which today's gate treats as mandatory for agent runs; prompt-injected pages would act with the user's real sessions. Any reopening needs an owner decision and an ADR first.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not carry this as a build recommendation. Record it as parked by owner ruling (2026-09-28, restated 2026-10-01) and list what would have to change to reopen it: an owner decision, the multi-backend abstraction (F-t2-059; AppState holds a single agent_driver today), a redesigned fail-closed gate that distinguishes interactive consented runs from background runs, and an attested relay in which Quarry validates every action against a BrowserBroker grant before the extension executes it. Measure how much of the need persisted profiles, human takeover and the secret bridge (F-t2-024) already meet before any spike.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: it needs an extension, a native host or hosted relay, a new executor kind, a gate redesign, store review and security review.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent, so it cannot be dropped as shipped, but it contradicts the owner's recorded ruling and the fail-closed egress gate; it should be moved out of the recommendation set into a parked or decision-record note that only an explicit owner reversal reopens.
